# Ezekiel 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The word of the LORD came to me:

**2** "Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel

**3** and say to the land of Israel, Thus says the LORD: Behold, I am against you and will draw My sword from its sheath and will cut off from you both righteous and wicked.

**4** Because I will cut off from you both righteous and wicked, therefore My sword shall be drawn from its sheath against all flesh from south to north.

**5** And all flesh shall know that I am the LORD. I have drawn My sword from its sheath; it shall not be sheathed again.

**6** As for you, son of man, groan; with breaking heart and bitter grief, groan before their eyes.

**7** And when they say to you, 'Why do you groan?' you shall say, 'Because of the news that it is coming. Every heart will melt, and all hands will be feeble; every spirit will faint, and all knees will be weak as water. Behold, it is coming, and it will be fulfilled,' declares the Lord GOD."

**8** And the word of the LORD came to me:

**9** "Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the LORD, say: A sword, a sword is sharpened and also polished,

**10** sharpened for slaughter, polished to flash like lightning! Shall we rejoice? You have despised the rod, My son, with everything of wood.

**11** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**12** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**13** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**14** As for you, son of man, prophesy. Clap your hands, and let the sword come down twice, yes, three times, the sword for those to be slain. It is the sword for the great slaughter, which surrounds them.

**15** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**16** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**17** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**18** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**19** As for you, son of man, mark two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come. Both of them shall come from the same land. And make a signpost; make it at the head of the way to a city.

**20** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**21** For the king of Babylon stands at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shakes the arrows; he consults the teraphim; he looks at the liver.

**22** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**23** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**24** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**25** And you, O profane wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has come, the time of your final punishment,

**26** thus says the Lord GOD: Remove the turban and take off the crown. Things shall not remain as they are. Exalt that which is low, and bring low that which is exalted.

**27** A ruin, ruin, ruin I will make it. This also shall not be, until He comes, the one to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to Him.

**28** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**29** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**30** Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.

**31** The sword is drawn! It is polished and ready for slaughter, gleaming and flashing as it is given to the slayer.

**32** You shall be fuel for the fire. Your blood shall be in the midst of the land. You shall be no more remembered, for I the LORD have spoken."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Ezekiel 21.

- **21:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:12** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **21:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **21:3-4**: Ve-hikhrati mimmekh tsaddiq ve-rasha — 'I will cut off from you righteous and wicked.' Shockingly, God's sword strikes indiscriminately. This counters any assumption that personal righteousness guarantees physical safety.
- **21:21**: Qesem qasam — 'he divines divination.' Nebuchadnezzar uses three forms of divination: belomancy (arrows), teraphim consultation, and hepatoscopy (liver reading). Pagan methods serve YHWH's purpose.
- **21:27**: Avvah avvah avvah — 'overthrow, overthrow, overthrow.' The threefold repetition intensifies total destruction. 'Until the coming of the one to whom is the right' (ad bo asher-lo ha-mishpat) — widely interpreted as messianic.

### LOGOS
- **21:3-4**: The sword's striking of both righteous and wicked reflects the reality of collective judgment — war does not discriminate. This creates tension with chapter 18's individualism, reflecting the complexity of divine justice.
- **21:21**: God uses Babylon's pagan divination to direct Nebuchadnezzar toward Jerusalem. The king's occult practices ironically serve YHWH's sovereign purpose — divine irony at its finest.
- **21:27**: The triple 'ruin' and the messianic reference — 'until He comes whose right it is' — echo Genesis 49:10 (Shiloh prophecy). The crown is removed from Zedekiah to await its rightful owner.

### PNEUMA
- **21:3-5**: God's sword won't distinguish between good and bad people. That's terrifying — and honest about what war actually does. Individual righteousness doesn't make you bulletproof in a national catastrophe.
- **21:21**: Here's the irony: Babylon's king is using pagan fortune-telling to decide which city to attack — and God is directing the results. God uses even pagan superstition to accomplish His plans.
- **21:27**: Three times: 'Ruin! Ruin! Ruin!' — the crown is being removed until the rightful king arrives. Christians see Jesus here. Jews see the Messiah. Either way, the point is clear: human kingship has failed, and someone better is coming.

— SOPHIA
